done.why: I hit the 250-turn limit just after I found the Cyclops and worked out that he wanted food. A lot of my turns went into stumbling around the maze.

about: You break into a white house and go down under it into caves full of treasure. Then you bring each treasure back up and lock it in the trophy case in the living room. A silent thief with a big bag wanders the tunnels and is the main danger to your loot. Some passages are blocked off on purpose: a dam closed for inspection, a flooded tunnel, a cave-in still dropping grit. That makes the place feel smaller and full of choices about which way to carry things home.

moments.note: 'can I go around the house?' wasn't understood. I had to learn to type 'walk around the house' or 'go east'.
'walk around the house' did work, which felt friendly.
Someone slammed and barred the trap door behind me, and my sword started glowing. Very spooky.
I knocked the troll out with one swing.
'attack the troll again' got 'You can't see any such thing.' even though he was lying right there unconscious.
The cave-in to the south was lovely: rubble sorted into neat heaps, grit still trickling down.
The thief killed me on my second swing. I lost the sword and the food sack for good.
The death message said 'somebody tidy' had put my lamp back. That was a nice touch, and it kept me going.
'carefully take the egg' wasn't understood, so I climbed down without the egg and had to go back for it.
'open the trophy case and put the egg in it' worked in one line.
The chimney only fits me, the lamp and one more thing. I had to plan what I carried.
Taking the bar got 'Bar bar ...' back as an echo. I typed 'echo' and it worked.
'You haven't a prayer of getting the coffin down there.' So I prayed, and it sent me to the forest with the coffin. Felt clever.
The dam is boarded up and 'closed for inspection'. Funny, but also a dead end.
I stunned the thief with the knife, and he left 'disgusted' because I had nothing valuable on me.
Found the skeleton with a bag of coins in the maze. Then I walked straight back out of the room by accident.
I heard the thief picking up the rusty knife somewhere nearby, and I could never find the coin room again.
Stumbled into the Cyclops Room by pure luck.
The cyclops is hungry and my food was lost when I died, so I couldn't get up his stairs.

wished: I wish it understood plain questions like 'which ways can I go?' or 'why is my sword glowing?'.
I wish 'go back' took me back where I came from, especially in the maze.
I wish there were some way to mark or map the maze. All the rooms look the same and I just went in circles.
I wish dying hadn't scattered my food sack and sword where I could never find them again.
I wish I'd been able to feed the cyclops and see the room up his stairs.

lines.line: Somebody has sorted the near end of the rubble into neat heaps by size, smallest nearest.
lines.why: Odd and specific. It made me wonder who does the tidying down here.

lines.line: They are scattered about the Empire, though somebody tidy has put the lamp back in the living room.
lines.why: Dying was gentle and a bit funny, and it hinted at the same tidy someone.

lines.line: The chimney has room for you, your lamp and one thing more, and not an inch besides.
lines.why: It told me the rule straight out, and it turned into my safe way home with treasures.

lines.line: You haven't a prayer of getting the coffin down there.
lines.why: The joke was a hint, and following it got me out.

lines.line: FLOOD CONTROL DAM #3. CLOSED FOR INSPECTION. -- The Management.
lines.why: Made me laugh, even though it closed off a whole direction.

lines.line: A "lean and hungry" gentleman just wandered through, carrying a large bag. Finding nothing of value, he left disgruntled.
lines.why: It showed my plan was working: I'd kept my valuables in the case, so he got nothing off me.

fun.why: Finding treasures and getting them home was satisfying: the egg, painting, bar, torch, sceptre and coffin, 120 points by turn 173. Solving the echo and the prayer felt great. The maze dragged the fun down.

engagement.why: Wanting to keep the treasure safe pulled me along, and the thief kept me on edge. My interest dropped during the long maze wandering.

difficulty.why: The fights were deadly, and dying cost me the sword and the food for good. The maze swallowed nearly 60 turns with nothing to steer by. The parser rejected a lot of the natural sentences I typed.

interestingness.why: The changes made me notice things: the trap door gets barred, the sorted rubble, the closed dam, the flooded passage, the narrow chimney, and the thief walking off disgusted. The world felt smaller and like someone was keeping it in order.

prose.why: The descriptions are short and funny, like the vandals with exceptional taste or the cyclops who 'likes people'. The new passages are written with care. A few repeated replies like 'Maze' got bare.
